description_full: Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte, S.A.B. de C.V., together with its subsidiaries, holds concessions to develop, operate, and maintain airports in Mexico. It operates 13 international airports in Monterrey; Acapulco, Mazatlán, and Zihuatanejo; Chihuahua, Culiacán, Durango, San Luis Potosí, Tampico, Torreón, and Zacatecas; and Ciudad Juárez and Reynosa cities. The company is also involved in leasing of space to restaurants and retailers. In addition, it engages in the operation of parking facilities; OMA Carga business comprising warehouses that provides cargo logistics services, such as storage, handling, custody maneuvers, loading and unloading, x-ray screening of exports, and other services; the Terminal 2 NH Collection Hotel; and the Hilton Garden Inn Hotel at the Monterrey airport; and non-permanent ground transportation. Further, the company provides aeronautical services, which include passenger, aircraft landing and parking, airport security, passenger walkway, and complementary services; car parking; checked baggage-screening services; and construction services. Additionally, it builds and operates industrial park at the Monterrey airport. Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte, S.A.B. de C.V. was incorporated in 1998 and is based in Mexico City, Mexico.

financial_summary: Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro  is a mid-cap industrials business with a $5.3B market cap on $828M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +24% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 31% against a 9% cost of capital — a 21-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $323M in free cash flow — roughly 39 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.26× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 6.1×.

Shareholder yield of 4.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 4.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
